claims.content: The customer wants to create a free JTVauctions.com membership account.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The customer wants to create a free JTVauctions.com membership account.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A new customer creates a free JTVauctions.com membership account.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The customer is not yet registered and starts the Register Customer Account use case.
scope_contract.success_boundary: A free JTVauctions.com membership account has been created.
in_scope_actions: Create a free JTVauctions.com membership account

claims.content: Customer
The customer is a new JTVauctions.com user and does not already have a membership account.
The customer has access to a valid email address and phone number.
The customer is accessing the JTVauctions.com website.
The use case is triggered when a new customer tries to create a new JTVauctions.com account.
The customer enters their First Name and Last Name into the designated text fields on Registration Page 1.
The customer provides an E-mail Address, verifies it by entering it twice, and creates a unique Member ID ('Handle').
The customer creates a password of 8 to 12 characters and verifies it by re-entering it in the 'Verify Password' field.
The customer selects a payment method (PayPal, Amazon Payments, or Credit Card).
The customer checks the box to accept and agree to the Terms of Use.
The customer clicks the 'I Want to Sign in Now!' button to complete the short registration process immediately without providing additional optional information.
The system sends an automated transactional 'Thank You' email instructing the customer to enable cookies and add the appropriate email address(es) to their whitelist or Safe Senders list.

Diverges from Step 6: instead of clicking 'I Want to Sign in Now!' to complete the short registration immediately, the customer may choose to proceed to Registration Page 2, optionally provide additional information such as billing/shipping addresses, shipping preferences, and email preferences, and then click the 'Finish Now' button to complete the full registration process immediately.
At main-flow step 2, if the Member ID ('Handle') is not unique in the database customer table, the registration cannot proceed.

At main-flow step 2, if the email address is already in use, the system notifies the registrant that the email address is already in use; the registration cannot proceed with the duplicate email. The system asks whether the registrant needs to reset the password for that account and, if the registrant indicates 'yes', generates an email with a temporary password.
At main-flow step 3, if the password is not between 8 and 12 characters, the input is invalid and registration cannot proceed.

At main-flow step 5, if the user clicks on the grayed-out 'finish now' button before checking the Terms of Use checkbox, a popup message will appear telling the user that they must read and agree to the Terms of Use before they can proceed.

At main-flow step 6, when a new customer tries to create an account, the Consumer Protection negative file is cross-referenced; if there is a match, the registrant receives the message: 'We are sorry, we are unable to create an auction account for you at this time. If you believe this message to be in error, please contact our Customer Service team at: 800-550-8393.'

missing_aspects: Continuation after the duplicate-email password-reset offer is undocumented: the outcome when the registrant declines the prompt, and the exit after the temporary-password email is generated.

Age-eligibility (EC-EF-017) and disabled-cookie (EC-EF-014) constraints are not tied to any main-flow step, so they are not authored as exception branches here; main flow may need explicit checks or preconditions for them.

The claim states the submit button is grayed out and cannot be used if the checkbox is unchecked, but EC-EF-010 specifies this applies to the 'I Want to Sign in Now!' button (browse now), while EC-EF-009 implies the 'finish now' button can be clicked (albeit grayed out) to trigger the popup. The claim conflates the behavior of two different buttons.

claims.content: A JTVauctions.com membership account has been created for the customer, and the registration process is complete.

If the full registration path on Registration Page 2 is completed via 'Finish Now', all provided optional information (billing/shipping addresses and shipping preferences) is saved to the customer's account profile.
The system sends an automated transactional 'Thank You' email instructing the customer to enable cookies and add the appropriate email address(es) to their whitelist or Safe Senders list.

If the short registration path is completed by clicking 'I Want to Sign in Now!', the customer is taken to the Sign In page; if they were previously browsing, they are returned to their last product details page, or if they were on the home page, returned to the home page.

missing_aspects: Evidence card EC-PO-000 asserts that the system displays 'Welcome Back!' after registration, but the source text (Page 37) associates this message specifically with the standard Sign In page for returning users. There is no evidence that the system navigates to the Sign In page or displays 'Welcome Back!' immediately upon *registration* completion; instead, evidence indicates specific navigation paths based on user choice ('browse now' vs 'finish now') or direct transitions to success messages.

citation_audit.description: Latest model-authored candidates after internal semantic grounding verification and DRA; aligned with delivered slots.
